1.text: The clamour of the excited spectators gradually fades behind you as you venture ever deeper into the gloom of the cave tunnel. Large crystals hang from the tunnel ceiling at intervals of twenty metres, radiating a soft glow, just enough to see where you are going. As your eyes slowly adjust to the near-darkness, you begin to see movement all around you. Spiders and beetles scurry up and down the carved walls, vanishing into cracks and crevices at your approach; rats and mice scamper across the floor ahead of you. Drops of water fall into small puddles with a sinister dripping sound that echoes through the tunnel. The air is cold, damp and heavy. After walking slowly through the tunnel for about five minutes, you arrive at a stone table set against the wall to your left. Upon it sit six boxes, one of which has your name painted on the lid.

2.text: The Scorpion manages to grip you in its pincers long enough to swing its segmented tail forward over its head and drive its venomous sting into you. The effect is fatal, and you collapse on the floor of the Arena of Death, wondering whether Throm will manage to win.

3.text: The Gnome shakes his head and says: "I fear you have not passed the Trial of Champions. The secrets of Baron Sukumvit's Deathtrap Dungeon shall remain hidden for another year, for you will not be permitted to leave this place. You have been appointed my servant for the rest of your days; you shall prepare and modify the underground labyrinth for future competitors. Perhaps in another life you will succeed..." In the total darkness, you fail to see the pipe curving downward. You slip and, unable to grip the slime-coated pipe, slide over the edge. Your screams echo through the tube as you plummet fifty metres to the bottom. You have failed the Trial of Champions. You crawl across the floor and find yourself in the lair of a tribe of TROGLODYTES. As you creep past them, your scabbard strikes a stone. Test your Luck.

You clamp the tube between your teeth and plunge into the water. Gripping one of the bridge pillars underwater, you remain absolutely still for ten minutes. When you finally decide the Troglodytes have gone, you surface and look around. There is nobody in sight, and you climb out of the river and cross the bridge to the north bank. In a shrill voice, he says: "Well, another stone for my garden. I am glad you have come to join your friends. I am a fair man, and so I shall ask you one question. If you answer correctly, you go free — but if your answer is wrong, I shall turn you to stone!" He giggles again, obviously delighted by your arrival.

In a small recess in the left-hand wall, you spot a length of bamboo standing upright. Picking it up, you notice it is filled with a clear liquid. Your throat is painfully dry, and you feel a little dizzy from the heat in the tunnel.

27.text: You walk over to the terrified man and cut the chain with your sword. He falls to his knees and bows, thanking you repeatedly. He says that four years ago he entered the Trial of Champions but failed. He fell into a pit and had to be rescued by a Trial Judge, one of the administrators of Baron Sukumvit's dungeon. He was then offered the choice of death or service as a lackey in the Deathtrap Dungeon. To survive, he toiled as a slave, until he could bear it no longer and attempted to escape. Alas, he did not succeed and was captured by the Orcs, the flying guards of the Trial Judge. As punishment, they cut off one of his hands and sentenced him to a year's imprisonment in this cell. You ask whether he has any information that might be of use to you. He scratches his head: "Well, I didn't exactly do well in here myself, but I do know that you need to collect gems and precious stones if you hope to escape. I don't know why, but that's the way it is." Without another word, the ragged prisoner bolts out of the room, turning left down the tunnel. You decide to press on northward and turn right down the tunnel.

As Judge of the Trial, it is my duty to Baron Sukumvit to allow only the most capable to continue. Therefore, I must prepare a test of intelligence and strength to eliminate one of you. Please do not try to dispose of me. It would be utterly foolish, for, as you can see, there is no obvious way out of this chamber, and only I know where the hidden exit lies. 364.text: As you wipe the Manticore's blood from your sword, you are startled to see a small man with a large nose leap out from behind one of the marble pillars. He wears a tight green tunic and appears harmless, though you are suspicious of the way he holds an opaque glass orb with a glimmering green light. "My compliments!" he says cheerfully. "My name is Igbut the Gnome, and I am the Trial Judge for your final test. Needless to say, my magical powers are great, so you should not attempt to attack me. Perhaps you have learned during your journey that gems play an essential role in the Trial of Champions. The iron door before you is the exit to victory, but there is only one way to open it. Three gems must be placed in the lock mechanism in a specific order. Each gem radiates an energy that will activate the mechanism — if you place them correctly, of course. I will help you to some extent, but first we need the right gems. Do you have an emerald?"

365.text: You tell Throm that killing the Dwarf will accomplish nothing, as you would never find the way out of the chamber on your own. You tell the Dwarf you are ready, and he beckons you to follow. Throm must await his return. A secret door opens in the chamber wall, and you follow the Dwarf into a small circular room. He closes the door behind you and hands you two bone dice, ordering you to throw them on the floor. You roll a six and a two: total, eight. 366.text: The temperature continues to rise, far beyond the limits of human tolerance. Lying on the nearly molten tunnel floor, you cannot regain consciousness. Your adventure ends here.

367.text: He eyes you suspiciously when you say you are a competitor in the Trial of Champions. You ask him what he does in the tunnels, and he tells you, somewhat reluctantly, that he is a servant of one of the Trial Judges — the controllers of the different parts of the dungeon appointed by Baron Sukumvit. After some conversation, he admits he would like to escape, but no one can leave the dungeon, as they might reveal the secrets of its construction. 372.text: You finally reach the warrior's body, but the moment you touch the jewel, both it and the warrior vanish as if by magic. The door slams shut behind you, and an ominous rumbling comes from above. You look up and see the ceiling descending. You run to the door trying to escape, but it is locked and there is no handle on the inside. The ceiling continues to lower, and you are forced to lie flat on the floor, trying to hold back the ceiling with your hands and feet. But the effort is futile, and you are crushed between the blocks of stone.

373.text: You clamber over the soft boulder, fearing you might be absorbed by it at any moment. It is difficult to pass over the thing, as your limbs sink into the soft shell, but at last you manage to reach the other side. Relieved to be on firm ground again, you head east.

374.text: You search the cavern but find nothing of interest. Throm calls out from behind you, saying he has found a leather bag beneath a pile of rocks. Opening the bag, Throm laughs loudly as a tiny mouse scurries between his fingers and escapes into a crevice between two boulders. Suddenly, you hear the sound of cracking rock: stalactites break loose from the ceiling, dislodged by the vibrations of Throm's booming laughter still echoing through the cavern. You shout for Throm to flee through the archway as the stalactites come crashing down. Test your Luck.

378.text: Feeling rather nervous, you take a deep breath and plunge into the dark pool. The north wall does not extend very far below the water's surface, and you decide to risk swimming beneath it. Soon you begin to feel short of air and are forced to surface. You try not to think about the possibility of being trapped in an old submerged tunnel and are relieved when you emerge and find fresh air. You are on the other side of the wall and can see the tunnel rising out of the water and continuing northward. Climbing out of the water, you check the contents of your wet backpack. Test your Luck.

379.text: Exhausted by the long duel, you drop to your knees. As you gaze upon Throm's motionless body, a bitter hatred for the Dwarf fills your heart. Somehow, you will avenge Throm. Consumed by rage, you do not notice the Dwarf entering the arena until he stands before you, a loaded crossbow aimed at your chest. "I know what you're thinking," he says calmly, "but don't forget that only I know the way out of here. Get up, it's time for you to leave." The Dwarf indicates that you should walk ahead of him. Back in the chamber, he goes to the north wall and pushes one of the stones that forms it. A door-shaped section of the wall swings open, revealing a tunnel illuminated by crystals. With the crossbow still aimed at your chest, the Dwarf smiles, saying: "Good luck."

Ahead, you see an underground river flowing from east to west across the cavern, and a bridge spanning from one bank to the other.

400.text: The moment you appear at the tunnel exit, a crowd roars and cheers. The people part to let you walk toward a small podium where, seated beneath a colourful bamboo parasol, sits Baron Sukumvit. He looks dumbfounded, as though he never expected anyone to emerge alive from the Deathtrap Dungeon. The secret of Fang has been revealed. As the Baron rises from his chair, you climb the steps of the podium, bow before him, and observe those cold eyes fixed upon you in utter astonishment. You smile awkwardly as he extends his hand to you. Amid the deafening roar of the people of Fang, Baron Sukumvit opens the coffer containing your prize of 10,000 Gold Pieces. He then places a laurel wreath upon your head and proclaims you Champion of the Deathtrap Dungeon.
